newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel stable as Bank of Israel buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Shekel stable as Bank of Israel buys dollars.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was almost unchanged against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Thursday after the Bank of Israel intervened in trading, dealers said.

"Trading was very quiet today. The only active player in the market was the Bank of Israel," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim. "The central bank had to intervene in trading (buying dollars) after the basket fell by seven percent below the diagonal rate."

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
Dealers said the central bank bought only about $17 million of U.S. currency in its first market intervention in five months.
"For the near term the basket will remain at the current level and the Bank of Israel will have to continue intervening in the market," the Hapoalim dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2480 shekels against 3.2470 shekels on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6139 shekels against 3.6145 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7949 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8040 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.0598 shekels against 2.0636 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2480 shekels.
